xref.title: 1958 Percy Phillips Home Recording – "That'll Be the Day" / "In Spite of All the Danger"
xref.body: An ultra-rare, two-sided 78 RPM disc from 1958, recorded by John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison, pianist John Lowe, and drummer Colin Hanton at the home of Percy Phillips, who specialized in "down and dirty" recordings in his front room. Side one features Buddy Holly's "That'll Be the Day," and side two contains "In Spite of All the Danger," the first-ever Lennon-McCartney recording. This record is owned by Paul McCartney and is estimated to be worth at least 100,000 pounds if it were ever to be sold. "The result was a two-sided 78 RPM disc with Buddy Holly's That'll Be the Day on Side One, and the first ever Lennon McCartney recording on the other, in spite of all the danger."

xref.title: Disastrous American Tour – January 1978
xref.body: Manager Malcolm McLaren's plan to "conquer America" with the Sex Pistols resulted in one of rock history's most disastrous road trips. Initially, the group's visa applications were denied, forcing them to cancel an important appearance on Saturday Night Live, where Elvis Costello was called in as a last-minute replacement. The drummer for Elvis Costello's performance notably wore a t-shirt that read "Thanks, milk," a sarcastic jab at Malcolm McLaren. McLaren made a bizarre miscalculation about American culture by routing the tour away from major cities and through the deep South, an area not receptive to punk rock values. "Instead, what he got was one of the most disastrous road trips in the history of rock."

xref.title: New York City (1979) – Genuine Canadian Punk Classic About Toronto Bands Making Road Trips to CBGB
xref.body: The Demics formed in London, Ontario in 1977 and regularly made the drive to Toronto to participate in the scene. Drummer Marcy Saddy later left to join the B-Girls. Their EP *Talk's Cheap* appeared in 1978 on Toronto's Ready Records, followed by an album in 1980. Their best-known song, "New York City," is a tribute to the Toronto punk bands — the Viletones, the B-Girls, the Curse, the Diodes, and others — who would regularly drive nine hours to New York City to play CBGB and couch-surf. xref.title: Chaotic New York Concert (May 15, 1980)
xref.body: Public Image Limited (P.I.L.), led by Johnny Lydon (formerly Johnny Rotten), agreed to play two nights at the Ritz in New York for a $12,000 fee, despite internal squabbles, drug abuse, and money problems. The band was in no shape to play, lacking a drummer (the sixth one quit) and a bass player (who had just walked out). They quickly hired a 65-year-old jazz drummer from a Broadway music shop. Instead of performing live, P.I.L. pantomimed along to their records, hidden from the audience by a large screen with their silhouettes projected by bright white lights. The 1,500 people in the audience were kept waiting in the pouring rain for over an hour, then discovered the band wasn't playing, and Johnny Lydon began taunting and insulting the crowd. This led to a rain of garbage, a storming of the stage, and the destruction of all equipment, with the gig ending after just 25 minutes. "The gig was killed after just 25 minutes."

xref.title: Band Name History – From Fecal Matter to Ed Ted Fred to Nirvana (March 19, 1988)
xref.body: Kurt's first band was called Fecal Matter (fall 1985). Subsequent incarnations included Brown Towel (sometimes misbilled as Brown Cow). The first Kurt-and-Krist performance was at a house party on March 7, 1987, as "Skid Row" (unrelated to the metal band), with drummer Aaron Burkhard. Names considered at the time included Batguano, Designer Drugs, Gut Bomb, Egg Flog, Fish Food, Puking Worms, Bliss, Whiskey Biscuit, Incompetent Fools, Poo Poo Box, Pen Cap Chew, Throat Oyster, Window Frame, Yin-Yang Valvstem, and Ed Ted Fred. They entered the studio on January 2, 1988, still as "Ed Ted Fred." The name Nirvana was first used at a show in Tacoma on March 19, 1988 — Kurt was studying Buddhism and liked that Nirvana meant a state free from pain, worry, and the troubles of the world, reflecting his ongoing stomach problems and the psychological damage of his parents' divorce. xref.title: Bill Berry's Near-Fatal Tick Bite (May 1989)
xref.body: While R.E.M. was on tour in Germany in May 1989, supporting the "Green Album," drummer Bill Berry fell severely ill shortly after arriving in Munich. Initially suspected to be bronchitis or measles due to a rash, his condition worsened with hallucinations and fluctuating consciousness. Despite doctors' panic and a "huge buffet of antibiotics," the cause remained unknown until one doctor's blind prescription of tetracycline proved effective. xref.title: Formation Origin - Pickup Basketball Game (1989)
xref.body: The band's genesis began in Seattle when Stone Gossard and Jeff Ament formed Love Company and sought a singer by circulating a demo. Jack Irons, a former Red Hot Chili Peppers drummer, received a copy of this demo and passed it to Eddie Vedder, a surfer and night shift worker at a Chevron tank farm in San Diego, after a pickup basketball game in 1989. Eddie then wrote lyrics to three of the demo's five songs, dubbed them onto a new cassette, and sent it to Seattle, leading to his invitation to jam with the group and the formation of Pearl Jam. "This cassette passed out of a gym bag sometime in 1989 might have resulted in the most profitable pickup basketball game ever played."

xref.title: Dave Grohl Joined Nirvana Because His Band's Bassist Broke Up with His Girlfriend (1990)
xref.body: Dave dropped out of high school to tour with DC punk band Scream for about three years. In the summer of 1990, bassist Skeater Thompson flaked out mid-tour in Los Angeles over the loss of his girlfriend, canceling multiple shows. Dave was left penniless (temporarily crashing with three female mud wrestlers) and doing cash tiling work for food money. He called Melvins leader King Buzzo (Kurt Cobain's idol), whom he'd met in Europe, who told him Kurt had a band needing a drummer. Dave flew to Seattle on September 21, 1990; four days later he auditioned and passed. Dave later wrote a song about Skeater Thompson called "Just Another Story About Skeater Thompson," available only on a cassette-only release made under the name "Late" in late 1990, titled *Pocket Watch*. "Dave has never forgotten Skeater Thompson and how thankful he is that Skeater had such bad girlfriend trouble."

xref.title: Drug Overdoses and Jonathan Melvoin's Death (1996)
xref.body: Within six weeks of the Smashing Pumpkins' 1996 World Tour beginning, drummer Jimmy Chamberlain and touring keyboardist Jonathan Melvoin overdosed on heroin in Thailand in February, and again in Spain in May, narrowly escaping death. Jonathan Melvoin was subsequently fired but remained with the band until the tour concluded, while Jimmy was placed on "double secret probation." On July 11, 1996, just before two sold-out shows at Madison Square Garden in New York, Jimmy and Jonathan went to the East Village to purchase "red rum," a highly potent form of heroin. At 4 AM the next morning, Jonathan, who was ironically trained as an emergency medical technician, died from an overdose. Jimmy awoke from his stupor and called the police, leading to official statements being given within hours. "Jonathan Melvoin O.D. on heroin in Thailand."

xref.title: Jimmy Chamberlain's Firing and Return (1996-1999)
xref.body: Five days after Jonathan Melvoin's death, Billy, James, and Darcy of The Smashing Pumpkins issued a statement announcing their decision to "sever our relationship with our friend and drummer Jimmy Chamberlain." They explained that for nine years they had "battled with Jimmy's struggles with the insidious disease of drug and alcohol addiction," which had "nearly destroyed everything we are and stand for," and confirmed they would "carry on without him." Jimmy was exiled from the band for three years, a period during which the Pumpkins' fortunes began to decline. In an effort to revitalize the band, Jimmy was eventually asked to rejoin, making his return on April 10, 1999, at St Andrews Hall in Detroit, where the band appeared in their familiar lineup for the first time since July 1996. "Today, we are very sorry to tell you that we've decided to sever our relationship with our friend and drummer Jimmy Chamberlain."

xref.title: Lawsuit Against Napster (2000)
xref.body: Metallica, notably with drummer Lars Ulrich as the public face, filed a lawsuit against Napster on April 30, 2000, after discovering their unreleased demo "I Disappear" and their entire catalog were being freely traded online. Lars Ulrich physically delivered a 60,000-page list of 335,435 alleged Metallica song pirates to Napster's offices. The band sought at least $10 million in damages, a ban for all users trading Metallica songs, and university crackdowns on student downloading. This action generated intense fan backlash, damaging Metallica's reputation as "rich rock stars, bullying fans." Despite this, Napster was ultimately shut down in July 2001 after settling with Metallica and Dr. Dre, confirming that its practices violated copyright. xref.title: Taylor Hawkins' Death (March 25, 2022)
xref.body: Foo Fighters drummer Taylor Hawkins died suddenly on March 25, 2022, in Bogota, Colombia, just before the band was set to headline a festival. At approximately 7:40 PM on that Friday night, a call was made from a Four Seasons property reporting a guest with severe chest pains, but EMS responders arrived too late. Officially, he died from complications related to an enlarged heart (cardiomegaly), which weighed 600 grams (compared to a normal 300 grams). Although his doctors were aware of his enlarged heart for years, attributing it to his active lifestyle of surfing, biking, and intense drumming, little other information regarding his death was released, due to an "airtight" news blackout imposed by the band and management. This lack of information fueled conspiracy theories, though sources suggested a congenital problem exacerbated by exhaustion, as Hawkins had reportedly been feeling "rough" in the months leading up to the South American tour. His death profoundly impacted Dave Grohl, the Foo Fighters, and millions of fans globally. "Taylor was dead. Officially, he died of complications involving an enlarged heart, something called cardiomagalley."

xref.title: Jim Gordon Death (March 13, 2023) – Died of Natural Causes in Psychiatric Prison at 77; Killed Mother in 1983
xref.body: Jim Gordon was a highly respected session drummer in the 1960s who played on dozens of recordings and performed with Eric Clapton in Derek and the Dominoes, including on the classic "Layla." He then developed severe schizophrenia — voices told him to starve himself, he couldn't sleep, was alcoholic, and received the wrong treatment. On June 3, 1983, a voice told him to attack his mother with a hammer and stab her to death with a butcher knife. He did. He was sentenced to prison and denied parole at least 10 times due to the severity of his mental illness; he remained in a psychiatric facility until he died of natural causes on March 13, 2023, at age 77. xref.title: Drum Programming Challenges on "Pyromania"
xref.body: For the album "Pyromania," producer Mutt Lange insisted on the latest technology for drums. Chris Berkett spent six weeks programming all the drums on a Fairlight CMI. This pre-MIDI process required converting the drummer's demo tapes into musical score and then typing every single event into the monophonic Fairlight using a mathematical music composition language. "And I had to write all that stuff out in score. Because it had to be converted to mathematical music language."

xref.title: Early Beastie Boys Member and Multi-Award-Winning Producer
xref.body: Kate Schellenbach is a drummer who was an early member of the Beastie Boys before their ascent to widespread fame. Beyond her musical contributions to bands like Luscious Jackson, she has forged a successful career in television production, including winning an Emmy Award as a segment producer on *The Ellen DeGeneres Show* and serving as a producer for *The Late Late Show with James Corden*. "She was once part of the Beastie Boys before they took off."

xref.title: Early Career - Tommy Ramone's Connection
xref.body: Tommy (Ramone), who later became the drummer for The Ramones, was a recording engineer who had previously worked with Jimi Hendrix. "And their manager, Tommy, a recording engineer who once worked with Jimmy Hendrix, took over on drums."

xref.title: Early Career as a Drummer
xref.body: Before gaining fame as Iggy Pop, James Jewel Osterberg was a drummer in Detroit in the mid-1960s. He backed Motown groups like The Shangri-La's and The Temptations when they played in Michigan, and also played in a local band called The Iguanas. "James Jewel Osterberg was a drummer from Detroit who had spent much of the middle 60s backing up Motown groups like the Shangri-La's and the temptations whenever they played around Michigan."

xref.title: Early Drumming Career – Motown Gigs
xref.body: In the mid-sixties, Iggy Pop began his musical career as a drummer for the Detroit band The Iguanas, playing gigs around Michigan and recording several songs. He was also hired locally by Motown acts like The Shangri-La's, The Temptations, and The Four Tops for their live gigs, as they toured with minimal musicians and hired bassists and drummers on location. He was known for being able to pick up almost any song within seconds. "Iggy was one of the guys These Motown acts would hire to play drums for them."

xref.title: Early Drumming Education – Joe Bonny and Lessons
xref.body: Larry Mullen started playing drums at the early age of nine. His first teacher was Joe Bonny, who was recognized at the time as Ireland's best-known drummer. Larry's mother supported his interest by purchasing a secondhand drum set for 17 pounds. Despite extensive formal lessons, he grew bored with the strict formality, rudiment exercises, sight-reading charts, and playing along to others' music. "his first teacher was a guy named Joe Bonny who at the time was Ireland's best known drummer and he taught Larry well."

xref.title: Early Drumming Talent
xref.body: Before forming The Stooges and becoming Iggy Pop, James Newell Osterberg (Jimmy) was known as a talented drummer, playing in his school marching band and later in several rock bands. His drumming talent was admired by the Ashton brothers. "They admired Iggy's town as a drummer. Not only did he play in the school marching band but he also eventually ended up in a couple of rock bands."

xref.title: Early Drumming and Pixies Opportunity
xref.body: Kelly Deal began playing drums at age eight and was nearly recruited to join the Pixies as their drummer alongside her sister. However, after spending time with the band, she concluded she "just didn't have the chops." "She was originally a drummer from the age of eight, and at one point she was almost drafted in to join the Pixies with her sister as the band's drummer, but after hanging out with them, she realized that she just didn't have the chops."

xref.title: Early Female Orchestra Drummer
xref.body: Marion Panky played drums for an all-female orchestra in 1916, marking her as one of the early documented female drummers in a performing group during a period when female musicians, particularly percussionists, were still a novelty. "Marion Panky played the drums for her group, the all-female orchestra in 1916."

xref.title: Early Punk Drummer and Quick Learning
xref.body: Paloma Romero, a Spanish-born drummer, became a key figure in the early UK punk scene. Inspired by the movement, she learned to play drums in just one week before joining The Slits, an all-female band she co-founded with two 14-year-olds. "The whole scene inspired her to learn how to play the drums. She says she practiced for a whole week to learn how to play them. And then she joined an all-female band with a couple of 14-year-olds and they became the slits."

xref.title: Early Rehearsals and Lineup Changes
xref.body: The Ramones' first rehearsal took place at Johnny's apartment with bassist Richie Stern, who quickly quit. A more formal rehearsal followed on January 24th, 1974, at the Performance Studio, with Jeffrey on drums, Johnny on guitar, and Douglas on lead vocals and bass. They were initially "terrible," unable to play their instruments well or covers, only knowing their own simple songs. Douglas quickly lost his voice, and Jeffrey, a loud but slow drummer, moved to vocals, leading to Tommy eventually taking over drums in July 1974. "They were not ready, not even close. They had next to no idea how to play their instruments."

xref.title: Early Tour Bus
xref.body: In their early days, Green Day's first tour bus was an old library bookmobile bought from the Phoenix School system. It was overhauled by drummer Tré Cool's father, Mr. Wright, who owned a small trucking company. Mr. Wright generously acted as the official driver for the band's first three tours. "Drummer Trakewool's father came in really handy back then because he owned a small trucking company and he overhauled this old library bookmobile that he had bought from the Phoenix School system."

xref.title: Engagement with Blues Musicians
xref.body: Downie frequently attended blues performances at Kingston venues like the Prince George, seeking out and talking with old blues acts such as Luther "Guitar" Johnson backstage. He would also smoke pot with Johnson and his 300-pound drummer, Ola May, in the girls' bathroom, used as a private dressing room. "Me and Gordowney would go to places, downtown in Kingston and watch old blues acts like Luther Guitart Johnson would play at the Prince George."

xref.title: Entry into Arkells and Professionalism
xref.body: Tim Oxford joined Arkells after attending audio school and networking through various pub gigs. He was introduced to the band by their previous keyboard player who mentioned they needed a drummer. His professionalism and working equipment (unlike the previous drummer's broken hi-hats) immediately impressed the band. He initially recorded a 5-song EP with them, some of which was done in his basement facilities. "Then when we met Tim, it was like, whoa, this guy is really professional because he was a very accomplished drummer, but his equipment also worked."

xref.title: Evolution of Bass Programming
xref.body: Peter Hook's later work in New Order involved programming bass lines and drum machines with drummer Stephen Morris. This collaborative approach significantly contributed to the band's unique sound, making it greater than the sum of its individual parts. "Later, his work in programming bass lines and drum machines with new order drummer Stephen Morris made that band into something much more than the sum of its parts."

xref.title: Exemplar of 1980s Drum Sound
xref.body: The band, featuring Robert Palmer, members of Duran Duran, and drummer Tony Thompson, is highlighted as a prime example of the pervasive drum sound of the 1980s. This sound was characterized by its big, boomy, and powerful quality, often achieved by recording in large, reverberant rooms and augmenting with electronic effects like gated reverbs. "The Power Station featuring Robert Palmer, a couple of guys from Durandoran and drummer Tony Thompson. That is an example of the drum sound that was very much invoked in the 1980s."

xref.title: Extensive Session Work
xref.body: Jim Gordon was a highly prolific drummer, contributing to literally hundreds of songs for a wide array of prominent artists including George Harrison, Joe Cocker, Dave Mason, Gordon Lightfoot, Harry Nilsson, Frank Zappa, Art Garfunkel, Traffic, and Steely Dan. He even contributed to the first Muppet movie. "Gordon could be heard on literally hundreds of songs."
